name: An accepted turn enters interpretation
description: The turn's first hop. It matches with eq rather than the transition operator because a transition condition needs a recorded previous value and returns false on an entity's FIRST evaluation (design F3) — and a turn entity is CREATED directly in `accepted` by intake's atomic create, so a transition-guarded rule would never fire for it at all.

name: A committed interpretation enters adjudication
description: Both a real casekeeper decision and the deterministic non-mystery no-op commit one case-decision reference. Rules branch on the pointer's arrival, never on action prose or private case content.

name: A verdict that calls for the dice enters resolution
description: The adjudicator's REPORTED roll gate routes the turn, never the advisory (plausibility, risk) mapping: the persona that read the fiction holds that authority (design D12). The phase condition is eq and not transition because the phase moved to `adjudicating` when the stage was ENTERED — the verdict lands later, with the phase unchanged, so a transition condition would be false at exactly the moment this rule must fire.

name: A verdict that declines the dice goes straight to application
description: The no-roll path (design D3): the verdict declared a single `auto` band and no roll-result triple is ever created for this turn. The applying phase admits `adjudicating` directly for exactly this reason.

name: A resolved roll enters application
description: The band the dice selected is matched against the closed roll-band set rather than tested for non-emptiness, so a turn carrying `auto` here — a band the dice cannot select — does not advance. The value set is verified against vocabulary.RollBands() when the pack loads.

name: Committed effects enter the companion stage
description: The applier lands the batch marker LAST, after every per-entity merge succeeded, so its presence is what says the world actually changed. A batch that was refused fails the turn instead, and a failed turn is terminal — it never reaches narration.

name: A companion stage result enters narration
description: Every companion path lands one exact structural stage record, including no bond, no trigger, and exhausted outcomes. Narration waits on that record and never on companion prose.

name: Landed narration closes the turn
description: This rule is why `*.ref` predicates stay rule-matchable. It branches on the ARRIVAL of a pointer at prose, never on the prose: a reference tells the pack that the narrator finished and tells it nothing about what was said. Flagging turn.narration.ref rule-opaque would fail this whole pack at load.

name: A completed turn is resolved
description: Here the phase MOVE is the event, so this is the one hop where the transition operator is the right guard rather than the wrong one — and its `from` set is verified against vocabulary.PhasePredecessors(complete) when the pack loads, so the FSM is stated once and the pack is checked against it rather than restating it.

name: A failed turn is resolved
description: The same notification for the other ending, because everything downstream of it owes the player an answer either way: the campaign ledger records failed turns alongside completed ones, and an egress adapter that only spoke about successes would leave a player waiting on a turn that already ended.
